case_title: Puran Chand v. State of H.P.
accused_victim_relationship: Not stated (defence alleged previous enmity with the victim's family; the court did not accept this and no other relationship is described)
statutory_provisions: IPC s.376; IPC s.506 Part I (referred to as s.506-1)
evidence_type: Victim's testimony; oral evidence of father (PW-2) and brother (PW-3); medical evidence of doctor (PW-5); age documents (birth certificate, matriculation certificate); circumstantial evidence (delay in FIR, victim's suicide attempt)
aggravating_circumstances: Victim was a minor aged 17; victim attempted suicide by consuming poison due to trauma of rape
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under IPC s.376 and s.506-1; sentenced to 7 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.5,000 (default 1 year simple imprisonment) under s.376; 3 months simple imprisonment under s.506-1
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld
offence_finally_established: Rape (IPC s.376) and criminal intimidation (IPC s.506 Part I)
neutral_facts: On 20 August 2006, at about 2 p.m., the victim, a 17-year-old girl who had taken goats to graze in a forest about half a kilometre from her village, was sitting alone on a footpath when the accused caught hold of her from behind. When she asked why, the accused did not respond. The accused physically abused her body, removed her clothes, made her lie on the ground and committed sexual assault by rape. She raised an alarm but no one came. After leaving, the accused threatened her with consequences if she disclosed the incident. Out of fear she did not tell her parents for several days, but remained tense and distressed. On 2 September 2006 she consumed poison, became unconscious and was taken to several hospitals, finally to a postgraduate institute, where she remained until 10 September 2006. On regaining consciousness she told her father and brother that the accused had raped her on 20 August. A first information report was registered on 11 September 2006, after which she was medically examined. The examining doctor recorded no fresh evidence of bleeding, tear or scratch over the vulva, only a slightly reddened area on the outer mucosa, and noted that the hymen was intact. The doctor also noted that the examination was carried out 21 days after the occurrence. The victim's age was established through a birth certificate, a matriculation certificate and medical age tests. The accused was arrested on 12 September 2006 and a charge sheet was filed. The victim's account was supported by her father and brother.
physical_harm: Victim consumed poison in a suicide attempt, became unconscious and was hospitalised until 10.09.2006; medical examination recorded no fresh bleeding, tear or scratch, and the doctor recorded the hymen as intact
motive: alleged: previous enmity with the victim's family (defence contention; not accepted by the court)
key_evidence_accepted: Victim's testimony of forcible rape; explanation for the 22-day delay in lodging the FIR; victim's immediate account to the doctor, father and brother on regaining consciousness; father's and brother's corroborating testimony; doctor's non-categorical denial of hymen rupture; birth and matriculation records proving minority
witness_credibility: Victim's version found reliable after cross-examination; father and brother corroborated her account; doctor had not categorically denied hymen rupture, so the medical evidence was not decisive
post_offence_conduct: Accused left the place and threatened the victim not to disclose the incident; no other post-offence conduct of the accused is recorded
custody_duration: Not stated (arrest on 12.09.2006 is recorded; duration of custody is not stated)
trial_duration: offence: 20.08.2006; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 29.09.2009; Supreme Court: 23.04.2014
legal_representation: Appellant: Amicus Curiae appointed by the Court (Anne Mathew, A.C., Rishi Maheshwari, R.V. Kameshwaran); State: Anil Soni, Anish Kumar Gupta, Deep Shika Bharati, R.D. Gupta
investigation_status: FIR No.186/2006 registered at Police Station Nahan on 11.09.2006 (per defence statement); victim medically examined; investigation completed by PW-9; accused arrested 12.09.2006; charge sheet submitted
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.376 and s.506-1, 7 years RI; High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence upheld (judgment dated 29.09.2009); Supreme Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence upheld
prosecution_argument: State supported the reasons of the High Court and trial court and relied on the evidence of PW-2 (father), PW-1 (brother) and related testimony, including the victim's immediate disclosure on regaining consciousness
defence_argument: Accused falsely implicated due to enmity; 22-day delay in FIR unexplained; suicide attempt due to examination fear, not rape; hymen intact per medical evidence; injuries mentioned by victim not recorded by doctor; sole testimony of prosecutrix should not be relied on
legal_principle_applied: Amended s.114-A Evidence Act (presumption of absence of consent) applied impliedly where victim attempted suicide due to trauma of rape; rape held proved even on attempt; delay in FIR adequately explained; medical evidence not decisive where other circumstantial evidence supports prosecution; sole testimony of prosecutrix accepted after cross-examination
sentencing_rationale: Not applicable (sentence upheld as imposed; no separate sentencing reasoning given)
judicial_aggravating_factors: None expressly weighed as aggravating; court stressed the victim's trauma and suicide attempt as reasons to credit her version
